name: Skolt Sami

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Skolt Saami (skol1241).

notes: Research. Skolt Sami is an Eastern Saami language of the Uralic family, written since 1973 (Feist 2010, Moshnikoff et al.) in a Latin orthography rich in special letters. The map covers the base Latin letters and the language-specific graphemes: â (near-open central vowel), õ (close-mid central vowel), ä and å, the caron letters č š ž, the barred/hooked consonants đ (ð), ǥ (ɣ) and ǩ (palatalized k), ŋ, and the doubled affricates ǧǧ/ǯǯ/ʒʒ, which the orthography always writes geminate and which realise as [ɟɟʝʲ]/[ddʒ]/[ddz] (single ǧ/ǯ/ʒ are given a non-geminate fallback). Word stress is fixed on the first syllable (Feist 2010). Two suprasegmental facts documented in the source grammars are known engine-limit gaps, not orthography gaps: (1) the acute accent ´ before a consonant cluster and the apostrophe ' mark the language's productive consonant-gradation palatalization/quantity alternation, whose surface realisation depends on the whole following cluster (testing confirmed a literal ´→ʲ mapping raises PER, since the mark's effect is cluster-wide, not a fixed one-to-one insertion); (2) Skolt Sami phonetically inserts an echo/epenthetic vowel after a word-final consonant or cluster, matching the word's vowel harmony, that the orthography never spells at all — there is no grapheme to attach that insertion to. Both are left unencoded here.
